title: GATE CY Topic Test: General Aptitude (GA) — Set 01
titleEn: GATE CY Topic Test: General Aptitude (GA) — Set 01

questions.questionTextEn: Neither the project manager nor the lead engineers _____ aware of the revised deadline until yesterday.
questions.explanationEn: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the noun closer to it. Because 'lead engineers' is plural and the time marker 'until yesterday' requires the simple past tense, the plural past verb 'were' is grammatically correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Thermometer : Temperature :: Barometer : _____
questions.explanationEn: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature. Analogously, a barometer is an instrument specifically used to measure atmospheric pressure (whereas hygrometers measure humidity and anemometers measure wind speed).

questions.questionTextEn: The board asked the auditor to look _____ the sudden discrepancy in the quarterly inventory report.
questions.explanationEn: The phrasal verb 'look into' means to investigate or examine a matter thoroughly, which fits an auditor checking a discrepancy. 'Look after' means to take care of, and 'look upon' means to regard.

questions.questionTextEn: Pointing to a photograph of a man, Meera says, 'He is the only son of my mother's father.' How is the man in the photograph related to Meera?
questions.explanationEn: Meera's mother's father is Meera's maternal grandfather. The only son of Meera's maternal grandfather is the brother of Meera's mother, who is Meera's maternal uncle.

questions.questionTextEn:
Statements: No reptile is a mammal. All snakes are reptiles.
Which one of the following conclusions is DEFINITELY TRUE?
questions.explanationEn: Since every snake belongs to the set of reptiles, and the set of reptiles is completely disjoint from the set of mammals, no snake can be a mammal. The converse 'All reptiles are snakes' does not follow.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid wooden cube has all six of its outer faces painted blue and is then sliced by $6$ cuts ($2$ cuts parallel to each pair of opposite faces) into $27$ identical smaller unit cubes. How many of the smaller cubes have ZERO faces painted blue?
questions.explanationEn: Slicing a $3 \times 3 \times 3$ cube produces $(n - 2)^3$ completely unpainted interior cubes. For $n = 3$, $(3 - 2)^3 = 1^3 = 1$ unit cube at the very center has zero painted faces.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid cube of side $10\text{ cm}$ is placed on a flat table. How many distinct planes of reflectional symmetry does a regular cube possess in 3D space?
questions.explanationEn: A regular cube has $3$ principal mirror planes parallel to pairs of opposite faces (bisecting opposite edges) plus $6$ diagonal mirror planes (each passing through a pair of opposite edges), for a total of $3 + 6 = 9$ planes of reflectional symmetry.

questions.questionTextEn: If $2^{x - 3} = 128$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanationEn: Since $128 = 2^7$, the equation becomes $2^{x - 3} = 2^7$. Equating the exponents gives $x - 3 = 7$, so $x = 10$.

questions.questionTextEn: The lengths of the two diagonals of a rhombus are $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$. What is the area of the rhombus (in $\text{cm}^2$)?
questions.explanationEn: The area of a rhombus with diagonals $d_1$ and $d_2$ is $A = \frac{1}{2} d_1 d_2$. Substituting $d_1 = 6\text{ cm}$ and $d_2 = 8\text{ cm}$ gives $A = \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers appearing on top is $9$?
questions.explanationEn: There are $6 \times 6 = 36$ equally likely ordered outcomes $(a, b)$. The pairs summing to $9$ are $(3, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4),$ and $(6, 3)$—a total of $4$ favorable outcomes. Thus, the probability is $\frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Passage: Urban green roofs absorb rainwater, reducing stormwater runoff into municipal drains during heavy monsoons. They also lower rooftop temperatures through evapotranspiration, decreasing the cooling load on buildings beneath them. However, older structures often lack the load-bearing capacity required to support saturated soil layers without costly structural reinforcement.
Which one of the following can be logically inferred from the passage?
optionsEn: Stormwater runoff increases when rooftop temperatures are lowered by evapotranspiration.
Retrofitting older buildings with green roofs may involve additional structural expenses.
Green roofs completely eliminate the need for air conditioning in urban buildings.
All newly constructed buildings are legally required to install green roofs.
questions.explanationEn: The final sentence explicitly notes that older structures often lack load-bearing capacity without 'costly structural reinforcement', directly implying that retrofitting them may incur extra structural expenses. The other options overstate ('completely eliminate', 'legally required') or contradict the passage.

questions.questionTextEn: Altruism : Selfishness :: Prudence : _____
questions.explanationEn: Altruism and selfishness are direct antonyms. 'Prudence' means careful foresight and good judgment in avoiding unnecessary risks; its direct antonym is 'recklessness' (heedless disregard of danger or consequences). 'Frugality' and 'cautiousness' are near-synonyms of prudence.

questions.questionTextEn:
Six colleagues P, Q, R, S, T, and U sit around a circular table facing the center.
(i) P sits second to the left of Q.
(ii) R sits directly opposite to Q.
(iii) S sits immediately to the right of P.
(iv) T is not a neighbor of Q.
Who sits directly opposite to S?
questions.explanationEn: Label seats $1$ to $6$ clockwise. Place Q at seat $1$; then R (opposite Q) is at seat $4$. Facing the center, 'left' is clockwise, so P (second to left of Q) is at seat $3$. 'Right' is counter-clockwise, so S (immediately right of P) is at seat $2$. The remaining seats are $5$ and $6$, and since T is not a neighbor of Q (seat $1$), T cannot sit at seat $6$; hence T is at seat $5$ and U is at seat $6$. Directly opposite to S (seat $2$) is seat $5$, where T sits.

questions.questionTextEn: In a family of six members (A, B, C, D, E, F), there are two married couples. D is the grandmother of A and mother of B. C is the wife of B and mother of F. F is the granddaughter of E. How is C related to A?
questions.explanationEn: D is the mother of B and grandmother of A, and F is the granddaughter of E, so D and E form the elder married couple (parents of B). B and C form the second married couple, and C is the mother of F. Since there are only six members (D, E, B, C, F, A) and D is grandmother of A, A must also be a child of B and C. Thus, C is the mother of A.

questions.questionTextEn: A fair balance scale (two pans, no weights) is used to identify $1$ heavier counterfeit coin among $27$ visually identical coins (the other $26$ have equal weight). What is the MINIMUM number of weighings guaranteed to find the heavier coin?
questions.explanationEn: Each weighing on a two-pan balance has $3$ possible outcomes (left pan heavier, right pan heavier, or balanced), dividing the candidate coins into $3$ equal groups. Since $3^k \ge 27$ gives $k = 3$ ($27 \to 9 \to 3 \to 1$), exactly $3$ weighings are both necessary and sufficient to guarantee finding the heavier coin.

questions.questionTextEn: A $3 \times 3$ grid of unit squares is drawn on a flat sheet (forming $4$ horizontal and $4$ vertical grid lines). How many RECTANGLES of all sizes (including squares) can be formed using the grid lines?
questions.explanationEn: Any rectangle in a grid is uniquely determined by choosing $2$ distinct vertical lines from the $4$ available and $2$ distinct horizontal lines from the $4$ available. Thus, the total number of rectangles is $\binom{4}{2} \times \binom{4}{2} = 6 \times 6 = 36$.

questions.questionTextEn: A fair six-sided die is rolled independently $3$ times. What is the probability of obtaining the number $6$ AT LEAST ONCE?
questions.explanationEn: Use the complement event (getting NO $6$ in any of the $3$ rolls). The probability of not rolling a $6$ on a single roll is $\frac{5}{6}$, so for $3$ independent rolls it is $\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^3 = \frac{125}{216}$. Hence, $P(\text{at least one } 6) = 1 - \frac{125}{216} = \frac{91}{216}$.

questions.questionTextEn: If $4^x - 4^{x - 1} = 24$, what is the value of $(2x)^x$?
questions.explanationEn: Factor out $4^{x - 1}$: $4^{x - 1}(4 - 1) = 24 \implies 4^{x - 1} = 8 \implies 2^{2x - 2} = 2^3 \implies 2x - 2 = 3 \implies x = \frac{5}{2}$. Substituting $2x = 5$ and $x = \frac{5}{2}$ gives $(2x)^x = 5^{5/2} = 5^2 \cdot 5^{1/2} = 25\sqrt{5}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid metallic sphere of radius $6\text{ cm}$ is melted and recast without loss into identical smaller solid spheres, each of radius $2\text{ cm}$. How many smaller spheres are formed?
questions.explanationEn: By conservation of volume, the number of smaller spheres is $N = \frac{\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3} = \left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{6}{2}\right)^3 = 3^3 = 27$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two cards are drawn sequentially WITHOUT replacement from a standard $52$-card deck. What is the probability that BOTH drawn cards are Hearts?
questions.explanationEn: There are $13$ Hearts in a $52$-card deck. The probability that the first card is a Heart is $\frac{13}{52} = \frac{1}{4}$. Given that, $12$ Hearts remain among $51$ cards, so the second probability is $\frac{12}{51} = \frac{4}{17}$. Multiplying gives $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{4}{17} = \frac{1}{17}$.
